result.analysis_summary: The athlete establishes rowing rhythm differently across the four work intervals. Work 3 at second 840 shows a slower and less-fluid restart compared to the other intervals, requiring more strokes to stabilize rhythm.

findings.comparison: Work 1 stabilizes after 3 strokes, similar to Work 4 but slower than Work 2.
findings.counterevidence: Works 1 and 4 show similar initial recovery timing but stabilize faster than Work 3.
findings.direct_observation: Recovery timing is slightly longer; hands-away occurs later relative to seat movement. Body preparation is visible but not fully synchronized with leg drive.
findings.limitations: Observation limited to visible stroke mechanics without physiological inference.
findings.title: Work 1 Start

findings.comparison: Work 2 stabilizes fastest, after 2 strokes, with smoother sequencing.
findings.counterevidence: Work 2 stabilizes fastest, with smoother sequencing.
findings.direct_observation: Recovery timing is consistent with Work 1’s initial strokes. Hands-away timing is slightly earlier than Work 1. Body preparation appears more anticipatory.
findings.limitations: Observation limited to visible stroke mechanics without physiological inference.
findings.title: Work 2 Start
